subject: Pilot launch commit — monthly ramp, conditional surge buffer, and per-token tiers
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@horizongames.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@horizongames.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot / launch commit question

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re finalizing the launch economics for our summer title and need clarity on two things before I brief procurement: 1) a monthly commit schedule that reflects our three-week marketing ramp (big spikes in Week 2 of each month for the first three months), and 2) whether Redwood will allow a small surge buffer and a conditional holdback if we cross the threshold for additional credits.

High level: we want a usage-based per-token discount for committed volume with a true-up at month end. Can you sketch an example schedule (month-by-month commit buckets + surge allowance + true-up logic)? Also if you can attach any short cost-model we can drop into our finance review, that’d be great.

—Elaine
Director of Platform Partnerships
Horizon Games

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Elaine Park <elaine@horizongames.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot / launch commit question

Elaine — thanks for the clear ask. I’ve put together an initial sketch and example cost model for your finance and procurement teams (attached). High-level proposal below; attaching a PDF + an editable XLSX.

Summary (proposal v1)
- Commit tiers (monthly): 1) 0-50M tokens (base) 2) 50M-200M (mid) 3) 200M+ (launch elite)
- Per-token pricing: progressive discounts at each tier (we show example pricing in the XLSX).
- Monthly ramp: we model a three-month ramp with Week-2 spikes. Monthly commits increase 40% month-over-month for the first two months, then level.
- Surge buffer: we can offer a 20% surge buffer over committed monthly volume that consumes a pre-funded credit pool (holds $X in credit until usage resolves). Any overage beyond surge is billed at overage per-token rate with a cap.
- Conditional holdback: for sensitivity, we propose a 10% conditional holdback of the surge credits that is refundable after the three-month launch window if aggregate usage meets projected curve.
- True-up: month-end reconciliation; if usage > commit + surge, overage billed; if usage < commit, no retro credits but we apply a credit toward next month for minor underutilization (up to 5%).

Attachments: Redwood-Proposal-HorizonGames-v1.pdf (PDF, 245KB); Cost-Model-launch-ramp.xlsx (XLSX, 88KB)

Next steps: 1) I’ve looped Monica (Customer Success) on logistics for metering/alerts. 2) If procurement wants a redline to the standard MSA for the holdback language, we can pull legal in. Would you like us to send a formalized proposal with explicit numbers and a DocuSign for signature?

—Kimberly
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Redwood pilot / launch commit question

Kim — quick internal. The 20% surge buffer + 10% conditional holdback is reasonable for a pilot but finance will want a little protection on the refundable piece. Suggest: 1) keep the 20% surge buffer, 2) reduce refundable holdback to 7.5% and tie refund to a simple 3-month cumulative usage test, and 3) include a 30-day rolling cap on cumulative overage billing so we don’t accidentally take open-ended exposure.

If you want to be more aggressive to close, we can front 50% of the holdback refundable immediately after month 2 if usage trend is on plan (sales discretion). I’ll approve the commercial if you keep the refund mechanics and cap in the doc.

—Rishi
Sales Lead — Enterprise Deals
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Elaine Park <elaine@horizongames.com>, procurement@horizongames.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Revised: Pilot launch commit — monthly ramp, conditional surge buffer, and per-token tiers

Elaine / procurement team — attaching a cleaned-up proposal reflecting internal feedback. Key changes from v1: holdback reduced to 7.5% refundable based on a 3-month cumulative performance test; 20% surge buffer remains; 30-day rolling cap on cumulative overage billing added; included example month-by-month commitment table.

Action items for you: 1) review attached and confirm whether procurement needs contract redlines or we can proceed with the proposal + DocuSign, 2) confirm the month-1 baseline tokens we should use for the committed schedule (we put a conservative 60M tokens as baseline in the XLSX).

Attachments: Redwood-Proposal-HorizonGames-v1.pdf, Cost-Model-launch-ramp.xlsx

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow if useful.

—Kimberly
Redwood Inference
From: procurement@horizongames.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Elaine Park <elaine@horizongames.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Revised: Pilot launch commit — monthly ramp, conditional surge buffer, and per-token tiers

Hi Kimberly,

The structure looks good. A couple of procurement asks before we sign: 1) can you clarify the accounting treatment of the refundable holdback (we need language for our auditors), 2) can we get a 60-day payment term (standard for us), and 3) is there an optional phased payment schedule tied to marketing milestones (we’d like to stage payments across the first three months).

If you can add the refundable-holdback accounting clause and accept Net 60, we can route the DocuSign for signature.

—Horizon Games Procurement

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: procurement@horizongames.com, Elaine Park <elaine@horizongames.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: Pilot launch commit — docuSign and next steps

Procurement / Elaine — thanks for the quick review. We can do the three items: 1) add an accounting-friendly refundable holdback paragraph (saying the holdback is held in a named credit pool and refunded as an applied credit on the invoice subject to the 3-month cumulative usage test), 2) accept Net 60 payment terms, and 3) include an optional phased payment schedule (Month 1: 30% of committed value due at signature, Month 2: 40%, Month 3: 30% — remainder billed monthly thereafter).

I’ve attached the final redline and the cost model, and included a DocuSign link here to execute once you confirm the phased schedule: https://na2.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=na2&acct=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000&PowerFormId=abcdef01-2345-6789-abcd-ef0123456789

If procurement confirms the phased schedule and Net 60, I’ll ask legal to lock the refundable holdback wording and send the PowerForm for signature.

Best —Kimberly
